newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs close higher, reforms little impact.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs close higher, reforms little impact.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed higher on Tuesday after a day of fluctuations as rotational buying of securities and construction shares outweighed early consolidation, brokers said.
They said financial reform proposals unveiled on Tuesday had little impact on the market as details had been widely leaked.
"Buying of securities and construction shares was mainly rotational. Perhaps the view that they are undervalued sparked interest," said Chung Chang-shik of Dongsuh Securities.
The composite index closed 7.67 points higher at 766.06.
The sub-index of securities stocks rose 6.32 percent to 1411.53, while that of construction shares increased 4.7 percent to 313.73.
In a presentation to President Kim Young-sam a panel studying financial reforms recommended increasing central bank independence and the bank's control over monetary policy.

The 31-member commission generally suggested giving more management autonomy to financial institutions and lifting various government regulations. "The draft was a huge-scale programme, which needs further deep study," said Lee Hahn-koo, president of Daewoo Economic Research Institute.
The commission proposed unifying the three financial watchdogs -- the Office of Bank Supervision, the Securities Supervisory Board and the Insurance Supervisory Board.

The commission also decided to uphold the current four percent individual shareholding limit in South Korean banks. However, it said the ceiling could be raised to 10 percent under certain conditions and with prior government approval.
Analysts said most of the proposals were indirect and would fall short of a Big Bang-type reform.
"I found nothing really new," said a Dongwon Securities broker.
